lp_h1: Understood at work. Understood at home.
lp_lead: A foreman's 20-second voice note becomes a simple Japanese and English instruction pinned to the machine. The machine stays locked until the worker proves they understood.
lp_problem_lead: Foreign workers are on Japanese shop floors, but instructions still arrive in a language many of them cannot fully follow.
lp_stat1: of employers say limited Japanese makes communication hard. It is the most cited challenge, up from 43.9%.
lp_stat2: injuries per 1,000 workers: technical interns 3.98, Specified Skilled 3.91, against 2.3 for all workers.
lp_source: Source: MHLW, Survey on Foreign Workers’ Employment 2025 (published 2026-08-31)
lp_gap_lead: Good tools already translate manuals and run tests. Of 22 products we checked, none do these two things.
lp_done1: カミナシ translates manuals and runs tests in 18 languages, Bengali included.
lp_done2: Teachme Biz runs tests and opens manuals from QR codes on site.
lp_only1: The Check gates one specific machine: the Machine Panel stays locked for that worker until they pass.
lp_only2: Every wrong answer tells the foreman which shop word was misunderstood, such as 玉掛け, and is written into the record a registered support organisation must keep.
lp_how1: The foreman records a 20-second voice note at the machine.
lp_how2: Each worker gets it in simple Japanese or English, with a Japanese back-translation the foreman can check.
lp_how3: The worker answers 2 or 3 questions. Each question tests one shop word.
lp_how4: The tablet beside the machine shows LOCK until the worker passes. No install: a QR sticker goes on each machine.
lp_life: Neighbourhood notices, such as garbage rules and drills, become plain steps with dates in the worker’s calendar. A Japanese Senpai links the worker to their street. A support log exports the support record for 特定技能 duties.
lp_course: Training that sticks: read it, watch it, drill it, inspect it.
lp_biz: Free for the company and its workers. Paid for by registered support organisations (登録支援機関).

home_h1: “Understood” is easy to say. Wakatta? makes it true.
home_lead: Wakatta? carries the conversation between foreman and worker back and forth until understanding is confirmed, so nobody has to say “I don’t understand” out loud.
home_problem_h: The most dangerous word on the shop floor
home_problem_story: Mr. Tanaka runs a small metal factory in Nagasaki. One morning he asks Rahim-san to change the die on Press #2. Rahim nods: “Wakarimashita.” By the afternoon, Rahim is injured. He had misread a single word, and neither of them knew until it was too late.
home_problem_why: Nobody was careless. A worker new to a country and a language can hesitate to ask again, so “understood” feels like the easiest answer. A JLPT certificate proves someone can pass a test. It cannot prove that one instruction, given in fast factory Japanese full of shop words, landed correctly.
home_problem_fix: The failure is in the connection between two people, so the fix belongs in that connection too.
home_stat1: foreign workers in Japan in October 2025, a record high.
home_stat2: more foreign workers in Nagasaki Prefecture in a single year, 12,807 in all. Manufacturing employs the most: 3,481 people across 2,338 workplaces.
home_stat3: foreign workers killed or injured at work in 2024, more than four times the 1,443 recorded in 2008.
home_stat4: injuries per 1,000 workers in manufacturing in 2021: foreign workers against all workers. Over twice the risk.
home_target: Japan’s 14th Accident Prevention Plan aims to bring the foreign-worker injury rate down to the national average by 2027.
home_sources: Sources: MHLW, foreign employment report (end of October 2025, published 2026-01-30); Nagasaki Labour Bureau, Nagasaki foreign employment figures (same date); Sompo Risk Management, Report 277 (2025-09-17), from MHLW data; MHLW, 14th Accident Prevention Plan.
home_today1: Copy the message, open a translation app, paste, read, switch back.
home_today2: The translation may be wrong, and the key word can still be missed.
home_today3: The employer never finds out, until the work is wrong or someone is hurt.
home_answer1: Each worker answers 1–3 quick questions. Green means understood.
home_answer2: Orange or red opens a Follow-up, and that one worker gets a simpler Re-explanation of the exact word they missed.
home_answer3: Nobody has to say “I don’t understand” out loud: the app asks for them, privately.
home_how1: The foreman speaks or types one instruction. The AI turns speech into text.
home_how2: Each worker gets it in their own language. The shop Glossary locks words such as 段取り or 金型交換, so they never drift.
home_how3: The AI writes short Check Questions and pulls out the Tasks. Nothing is sent until the foreman approves the draft.
home_how4: Workers answer. The foreman sees at a glance who truly understood.
home_f1: Tasks found in a message go straight to a shared Task Board, with assignees, deadline and machine.
home_f2: At a machine, the worker scans its QR code, reads the instructions and passes a Check. Only then does the machine show Ready; until then it stays Locked.
home_f3: A Daily Briefing shows who understood, who only opened it and who has not seen it. Push notifications bring new messages.
home_f4: Workers report Near-misses with a photo. Ask Wakatta answers from the shop’s own notes and flags emergencies.
home_diff1: Translation tools stop at translating. Wakatta? checks the answer and repairs the gap.
home_diff2: A machine unlocks only after its Check is passed.
home_diff3: One spoken message becomes clear text, questions and tasks.
home_diff4: Workers never have to admit confusion in front of others; the app asks on their behalf, privately.
home_built1: Android app: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, 15 feature modules, a signed APK.
home_built2: Web app: React and TypeScript, for the foreman’s PC and this page.
home_built3: Backend: Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL, live on Microsoft Azure.
home_built4: AI: Groq Whisper turns speech into text; Gemini translates, writes the questions and finds the tasks. Every AI step has a fallback.
home_built5: The Android app speaks Japanese, English and Bengali.
home_quality1: 30 of 30 evaluation cases passed for machine notes, notices and worker questions.
home_quality2: Chat messages: a valid draft in 10 of 10 cases, fully correct in 7 of 10. That is why the foreman reviews every draft before it is sent.
home_team_lead: In three days, five of us worked in parallel through a shared board of 27 cross-team requests, so frontend, backend and AI moved together.
